summary: Frontend-only testing of BATCH A1 (Evidence Locker audio-session fix: mic-lease-before-setAudioModeAsync ordering + TTS fail-closed guard). Static code review confirms the ordering fix (claimMic/withMicLease BEFORE every setAudioModeAsync call) is correctly implemented in all 5 listed files (app/(tabs)/index.tsx chat mic + 3 TTS/cleanup sites, app/fir-draft/index.tsx, app/intake/[token].tsx, app/(tabs)/lookup.tsx, app/visitor/interpreter.tsx) and the TTS fail-closed guard (isMicHeldByEvidenceLocker check before setAudioModeAsync) is correctly placed in src/hooks/useScreenSpeech.ts and app/fir-draft/index.tsx's speak(). However, live browser testing uncovered a CRITICAL, PRE-EXISTING bug (confirmed via `git status` NOT part of this batch's diff -- app/women/evidence-locker.tsx is untouched) that makes the entire acceptance scenario impossible to validate as intended and defeats the safety goal of this batch: navigating away from the Evidence Locker screen while a recording is actively in progress -- using ONLY the normal back button, touching NO other mic/TTS feature at all -- silently STOPS and DISCARDS the recording (app/women/evidence-locker.tsx's useFocusEffect blur-cleanup calls cancel(), which calls releaseLockerClaim() + recorder.stop() + discardTemporaryRecording() whenever active.current is true). Reproduced twice: started recording (confirmed via live timer 'Recording · 2s · 0 segment(s) saved'), tapped back once, waited, returned to Evidence Locker -> PIN gate reappeared, 'Ready to record', 0 saved items, discard button gone -- the in-progress recording was gone, not merely paused. This directly contradicts EvidenceRecorderProvider.tsx's own documented design intent ('mounted at the root layout level so recording survives navigation'). Practical consequence for this batch's acceptance test: a user/tester CANNOT be 'actively recording in Evidence Locker' AND 'on the Home/FIR-draft/Lookup/Interpreter screen pressing its mic' at the same time in this single-screen mobile UI, because simply leaving the Locker screen to reach any other screen already destroys the recording -- independent of, and before, the mic-lease ordering fix under test ever gets exercised. This also explains an initial false-negative in my own testing: pressing the Home chat mic after navigating away from an 'active' Locker recording succeeded with NO busy alert, not because the ordering fix failed, but because the Locker's arbiter claim had already been silently released by the blur-cleanup by the time I reached the chat mic. By contrast, app/(tabs)/index.tsx has an explicit code comment confirming chat_mic was deliberately designed to survive navigation ('Tabs stay mounted: unmount-only cleanup does not stop the microphone') -- making Evidence Locker's behavior an inversion of the stated safety priority (the most safety-critical recorder is the only one that does NOT survive navigation). Login/consent/language onboarding flow, Evidence Locker PIN creation/unlock, and recording start all work correctly in isolation. Did not reach a deterministic test of the FIR-draft mic-busy alert or any TTS-blocked notice end-to-end (FIR draft's mic button only renders after selecting an incident-type card, and further navigation attempts risked repeating the same selector-hunting loop) -- these were verified by static code review only. Unit test file src/voice/core/__tests__/micArbiterGuard.test.ts was reviewed and its logic/assertions are sound against the arbiter implementation; did not independently re-run it under node --experimental-strip-types (time-boxed), but the main agent's claim of a pre-existing ESM extensionless-import issue (shared with the already-existing voiceCore.test.ts) is plausible and not something I disprove.

integration_issues.flow: Evidence Locker recording survives navigation (app/women/evidence-locker.tsx useFocusEffect blur cleanup)
integration_issues.issue: CRITICAL, pre-existing (not part of this batch's diff per `git status`): navigating away from the Evidence Locker screen while actively recording -- via the plain back button, with NO other mic/TTS feature touched -- silently stops AND discards (discardTemporaryRecording) the in-progress recording and releases the arbiter's 'evidence_locker' claim. This contradicts EvidenceRecorderProvider.tsx's documented design that recording 'survives navigation', and makes BATCH A1's own acceptance test ('start Locker recording, then while it is actively recording try each of the other mic/TTS features') physically impossible to execute in the UI, since reaching any other screen to try its mic/TTS button already destroys the Locker recording first. The mic-lease ordering fix under test is code-correct but currently unverifiable end-to-end because of this separate, more severe bug.

action_items: URGENT, separate from this batch but blocking its validation: fix app/women/evidence-locker.tsx so recording does NOT stop/discard on screen blur (useFocusEffect cleanup currently calls cancel() unconditionally when active.current is true on navigation away). Evidence recording must persist across navigation exactly as EvidenceRecorderProvider.tsx already intends (mirror the 'Tabs stay mounted: unmount-only cleanup does not stop the microphone' pattern already used in app/(tabs)/index.tsx for chat_mic) -- otherwise the single-owner-mic-arbiter safety goal of this whole feature area is moot in real usage (a user can never leave the Locker screen while legitimately recording, e.g. to silence a phone call prompt elsewhere, without losing the evidence).

Once recording-survives-navigation is fixed, re-run the full BATCH A1 acceptance matrix exactly as specified (home chat mic, FIR draft mic, intake mic, lookup mic, interpreter mic, all 'Listen' TTS buttons) while Evidence Locker genuinely keeps recording in the background -- this could not be validated this round due to the blocking bug above.
Physical iOS/Android device testing is still required for the actual setAudioModeAsync/AVAudioSession behavior -- this cannot be verified in web preview regardless of the above fix.

Confirm FIR draft's mic-busy alert and TTS-blocked notice end-to-end once a stable in-progress Locker recording can be maintained across screens; this iteration only verified them by static code review (order of claimMic/withMicLease vs setAudioModeAsync, and isMicHeldByEvidenceLocker guard placement, all look correct in app/fir-draft/index.tsx, app/(tabs)/lookup.tsx, app/visitor/interpreter.tsx, app/intake/[token].tsx, src/hooks/useScreenSpeech.ts).
critical_code_review_comments: micArbiterGuard.ts (withMicLease, isMicHeldByEvidenceLocker, claimMic) is well-structured, flag-gated correctly (MIC_ARBITER_ENABLED, MIC_LEASE_GUARD_ENABLED), and withMicLease's throw-path release (lease.release() in catch before rethrow) correctly prevents a leaked lease -- matches the unit test's assertion.

Call-order fix verified correct by grep across all 5 touched files: claimMic()/withMicLease() is invoked before every setAudioModeAsync({allowsRecording:true/false...}) call site, including the three TTS/cleanup sites in app/(tabs)/index.tsx and the speak()/cleanup paths in app/fir-draft/index.tsx.

Inconsistent mic-survives-navigation behavior across the codebase is a real architectural smell: app/(tabs)/index.tsx explicitly engineers chat_mic to survive tab navigation, but app/women/evidence-locker.tsx -- the one recorder the whole arbiter system is built to protect -- does the opposite (cancels on blur). This asymmetry should be fixed before BATCH A1 can be considered safety-verified.

rca_of_issue: app/women/evidence-locker.tsx's useFocusEffect (around line ~326-363) returns a cleanup function that always calls cancel() on blur/unmount. cancel() checks `active.current`; when true (a recording is in progress), it sets active.current=false, calls releaseLockerClaim() (which releases the arbiter's 'evidence_locker' claim via EvidenceRecorderProvider), and calls recorder.stop().then(() => discardTemporaryRecording(recorder.uri)) -- i.e. it both stops AND discards the file, not merely pauses it. Since Evidence Locker is a stack screen (app/women/evidence-locker.tsx, not under the (tabs) group), any navigation to another tab/screen blurs (and on web, often unmounts) it, firing this cleanup. This is inconsistent with EvidenceRecorderProvider.tsx's explicit design comment that the recorder is hoisted to root layout specifically so 'recording survives navigation' -- that provider-level persistence is being defeated by the screen's own cleanup logic. This bug is NOT part of BATCH A1 (confirmed via `git status`: app/women/evidence-locker.tsx is not in the list of modified files) but it directly blocks verifying BATCH A1's stated acceptance criteria, since the test scenario requires the Locker to still be recording *after* the user has navigated to a different screen to try another feature's mic/TTS button.
